title: Electron Gain Enthalpy (Δ_eg H) & Electronegativity Scales
topics: Electron Gain Enthalpy (Δ_eg H) & Exothermic vs Endothermic Steps
Why Second Electron Gain Enthalpy (Δ_eg H₂) is Always Endothermic (+780 kJ/mol)
Halogen Anomaly (Cl > F > Br > I) & Group 16 Anomaly (S > Se > Te > Po > O)
Mulliken Scale (χ_M = (IE + EA) / 2) & Conversion to Pauling (χ_P = χ_M / 2.8)
quickSummary: Chlorine possesses the most negative electron gain enthalpy (Cl > F), and second electron gain enthalpies are always endothermic (O⁻ + e⁻ → O²⁻ is +780 kJ/mol). Electronegativity is quantified via Pauling, Mulliken, and Allred-Rochow scales.
summary: Master electron gain enthalpy anomalies, 2nd step endothermicity, and mathematical formulations of Pauling, Mulliken, and Allred-Rochow electronegativity scales.

summaryBox.title: Electron Gain Enthalpy
summaryBox.takeaway: Cl (-349 kJ/mol) has more negative Δ_eg H than F (-328 kJ/mol). Second electron gain enthalpy (Δ_eg H₂) is ALWAYS endothermic for all elements.

conceptBreakdown.content:
The enthalpy change when an electron is added to an isolated neutral gaseous atom:

$$\text{X}(g) + e^- \xrightarrow{\Delta_{\text{eg}} H_1} \text{X}^-(g)$$

• **Second Electron Gain Enthalpy ($\Delta_{\text{eg}} H_2$)**: **ALWAYS ENDOTHERMIC ($\Delta > 0$)** without exception due to severe electrostatic repulsion between incoming electron and the negative anion:

$$\text{O}^-(g) + e^- \xrightarrow{\Delta_{\text{eg}} H_2 = \mathbf{+780\text{ kJ/mol}}} \text{O}^{2-}(g)$$

• **Halogen Anomaly**: Chlorine has a MORE negative $\Delta_{\text{eg}} H$ than Fluorine because $\text{F}$ has a compact $2p$ subshell with high electron density, generating intense repulsions against incoming electrons:
$$\mathbf{\text{Halogen Order: } \text{Cl } (-349) > \text{F } (-328) > \text{Br } (-325) > \text{I } (-295\text{ kJ/mol})}$$

• **Group 16 Anomaly**: Oxygen has the LEAST negative $\Delta_{\text{eg}} H$ in Group 16:
$$\mathbf{\text{Group 16 Order: } \text{S } (-200) > \text{Se } (-195) > \text{Te } (-190) > \text{Po } (-174) > \text{O } (-141\text{ kJ/mol})}$$

χ_A - χ_B = 0.102 √Δ                                              χ = 0.359 (Z_eff / r²) + 0.744
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **Pauling Scale**:
$$\mathbf{\chi_A - \chi_B = 0.102 \sqrt{\Delta \text{ (in kJ/mol)}} = 0.208 \sqrt{\Delta \text{ (in kcal/mol)}}}$$
$$\Delta = E_{A-B} - \sqrt{E_{A-A} \cdot E_{B-B}}$$
Top Electronegative Elements: $\mathbf{\text{F } (4.0) > \text{O } (3.5) > \text{N } (3.0) \approx \text{Cl } (3.0) > \text{Br } (2.8) > \text{I } (2.5) \approx \text{C } (2.5) \approx \text{S } (2.5)}$.

2. **Mulliken-Jaffé Scale**:
$$\mathbf{\chi_M = \frac{\text{IE} + \text{EA}}{2} \quad (\text{in eV})} \implies \mathbf{\chi_P \approx \frac{\chi_M}{2.8} = \frac{\text{IE} + \text{EA}}{5.6} \quad (\text{in eV})} = \frac{\text{IE} + \text{EA}}{540} \quad (\text{in kJ/mol})$$

3. **Allred-Rochow Scale**:
$$\mathbf{\chi_{\text{AR}} = 0.359 \frac{Z_{\text{eff}}}{r^2} + 0.744}$$

quickRevision: Cl (-349 kJ/mol) has more negative Δ_eg H than F (-328 kJ/mol).
Δ_eg H₂ is always endothermic (O⁻ + e⁻ → O²⁻ is +780 kJ/mol).
Mulliken conversion: χ_P = χ_M / 2.8 = (IE + EA) / 5.6 (in eV).
